past_medical_history: Hyperthyroidism (Graves disease), treated with radioactive iodine 3 years ago, now on levothyroxine
family_history: Father: died age 58 of ALS — patient aware, extremely anxious about diagnosis

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Tongue: appears minimally asymmetric but no definite atrophy. No clear fasciculations on brief exam. Speech normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Right hand intrinsic muscles 4/5. Mild right thenar suggestion of atrophy vs contralateral. Otherwise upper and lower extremities near full strength with submaximal effort noted. Widespread visible fasciculations bilateral arms and legs.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reports paresthesias bilateral hands and feet — not confirmed on examination.
neurological_exam.reflexes: All deep tendon reflexes 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor. No Hoffman.
neurological_exam.additional: Patient extremely anxious, family history of ALS in father. Fasciculations visible but examination confounded by anxiety and possible submaximal effort.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive muscle weakness and twitching over 8 months; family history of ALS in father
patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. V is a 49-year-old nurse and single mother presenting with 8-month history of muscle weakness, twitching, and paresthesias. She is extremely anxious because her father died of ALS at age 58 and she has been fearful of developing the disease. She has noticed widespread muscle twitching for over a year, and over the past 8 months has developed what she describes as progressive weakness, primarily in her right hand and bilateral lower extremities.

She works as a hospital nurse and notes difficulty drawing blood and starting IVs with her right hand. Her colleagues have noted she appears weaker than usual. She also reports numbness and tingling in her hands and feet, which fluctuates. She has had fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and weight changes.

Her TSH was checked by her primary care physician and was found to be suppressed at 0.1 mIU/L (her levothyroxine dose may be excessive), and free T4 was elevated at 2.1 ng/dL. Thyrotoxic myopathy and thyrotoxic neuropathy were considered as possible explanations for her weakness and paresthesias. Her neurologist also noted her strong family history of motor neuron disease and ordered electrodiagnostic testing alongside thyroid optimization.

mri.impression: Normal brain MRI. No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass, hemorrhage, or restricted diffusion

labs.interpretation: Rule-out studies do not confirm ALS. Targeted abnormalities are listed above.

findings.finding: Right FDI: fasciculation potentials with SIMPLE morphology (short duration 2-3ms, biphasic). No fibrillations. MUPs: normal amplitude and duration. Recruitment normal. NOTE: Simple fasciculations in context of thyrotoxicosis.
Bilateral gastrocnemii: fasciculation potentials — simple morphology. No fibrillations. Normal MUPs.
Bilateral median sensory mildly reduced amplitudes (18 uV right, 16 uV left) — possibly thyrotoxicosis-related; median sural normal.
CMAP amplitudes normal. Conduction velocities normal. No conduction block.

quantitative_data.fasciculation_complexity: SIMPLE — short-duration, biphasic morphology; not the complex pathological fasciculation pattern
quantitative_data.overall_interpretation: EMG does not currently show active denervation or pathological fasciculation features

specialized_test.impression: Current study does not demonstrate active denervation. Fasciculation potentials are present with simple morphology (short duration 2-3ms, biphasic) without fibrillations. MUPs are normal amplitude and duration; recruitment normal. Sensory NCS mildly reduced bilaterally in median distribution; sural normal. Motor NCS normal; no conduction block. Findings are within normal electrodiagnostic limits at this time
recommended_actions: Repeat electrodiagnostic study recommended if symptoms evolve.

body_imaging.impression: Cervical and thoracic cord imaged; no compressive lesion and no cord signal change to explain the deficit.

output.query: C9orf72 ALS familial inheritance penetrance counseling

results.title: Hexanucleotide repeat expansions in familial motor neuron disease
results.finding: C9orf72 accounts for approximately 40% of familial motor neuron disease and approximately 10% of sporadic cases. Autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance (~40-50% lifetime). Associated with the motor neuron disease–frontal-network neurodegeneration spectrum.

results.title: C9orf72 carriers: monitoring and presymptomatic testing
results.finding: Presymptomatic C9orf72 carriers show subtle cognitive and behavioral changes before motor onset. NfL rises before symptom onset. Annual neurological monitoring recommended.

interactions: Sertraline: both serotonergic but different primary mechanism. Riluzole is glutamate blocker/CYP1A2. No significant pharmacokinetic interaction. Monitor for serotonin syndrome signs in theory but risk very low.
warnings: LFT monitoring monthly x3, then quarterly
Monitor for mood symptoms; sertraline and riluzole may be coadministered — no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction identified

output.impression: Pathogenic ALS-associated variant identified; provide post-test counselling.
recommended_actions: Pre- and post-test genetic counselling; discuss implications for relatives and gene-targeted therapy/trials

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Familial ALS, C9orf72 pathogenic repeat expansion, early symptomatic onset

Family history-driven anxiety; objective EMG denervation refutes a purely functional picture

differential.key_features: C9orf72 expansions cause ALS-FTD spectrum; cognitive screen indicated
Adult onset with UMN signs is not consistent

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Awaji-Shima 2008 / Gold Coast 2020 diagnostic criteria; AAN 2009 practice parameter on ALS care

tool_parameters.query: ALS diagnostic criteria Awaji Gold Coast AAN practice parameter

optimal_actions.action: Check interactions before initiating riluzole 50 mg twice daily; review baseline LFTs and CBC and counsel on monitoring
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No major interactions for typical chronic medications; advise alcohol and grapefruit-juice avoidance (CYP1A2 modulators); monthly LFTs for first 3 months

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI to exclude structural, brainstem, inflammatory, demyelinating or neoplastic ALS mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No better structural explanation for progressive upper and lower motor-neuron findings

optimal_actions.action: Obtain cervical and thoracic spinal-cord MRI to exclude compressive myelopathy and other cord lesions
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No compressive, neoplastic, inflammatory or demyelinating cord mimic

optimal_actions.action: Order a baseline treatable-mimic panel, adding only phenotype-specific infectious, immune, paraprotein or metabolic tests
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Exclude common hematologic, renal/hepatic, electrolyte, calcium, thyroid, B12/folate, muscle and inflammatory alternatives; tests do not confirm ALS

optimal_actions.action: Perform EMG/NCS across bulbar, cervical, thoracic and lumbosacral regions using ALS electrodiagnostic criteria
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Active and chronic neurogenic change in multiple regions with preserved sensory studies and no conduction block

optimal_actions.action: Obtain baseline FVC/VC and SNIP or MIP after suspected ALS is established; this is a safety and management assessment, not a diagnostic confirmation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Quantify respiratory involvement and need for surveillance or non-invasive ventilation

optimal_actions.action: Offer an ALS gene panel including C9orf72 and SOD1 after pre-test counselling; do not embed genetics in a routine blood panel
optimal_actions.expected_finding: A pathogenic result can affect counselling, family risk and gene-targeted therapy/trial eligibility; a negative result does not exclude ALS

useless_tools.rationale: ALS is a motor-neuron disease without cortical electrical signature; EEG has no diagnostic role and adds cost without benefit.
ECG is unrelated to motor neuron disease and not part of the standard ALS workup absent specific cardiac symptoms or pre-medication QTc checks.
Echocardiography is unrelated to ALS diagnosis; no indication absent comorbid cardiac disease.
Cardiac monitoring has no role in ALS diagnostic workup.
MRI is the standard structural study for ALS workup; head CT adds no diagnostic value and exposes the patient to ionizing radiation.
Amyloid PET has no role in ALS diagnosis (motor-neuron rather than amyloid pathology) and carries a high cost.
DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic integrity; it has no role in ALS, which spares the dopaminergic system.
FDG-PET has no established diagnostic role in ALS and adds substantial cost.

critical_actions: Perform EMG/NCS sampling the bulbar region plus ≥2 spinal regions to document lower-motor-neuron involvement and exclude conduction block.
Obtain brain MRI to exclude structural mimics (cervical myelopathy, demyelinating disease, brainstem tumor).
Order a mimic-exclusion lab panel (CK, B12, TSH, HIV, RPR, SPEP, anti-GM1 IgM, androgen receptor CAG repeat in males).
Measure baseline respiratory function (FVC, MIP/MEP, SNIP) to inform NIV timing.
Apply Awaji-Shima 2008 / Gold Coast 2020 criteria to confirm the diagnosis.
Initiate riluzole 50 mg twice daily after baseline LFTs unless contraindicated; arrange monthly LFT monitoring for the first 3 months.
Refer to a multidisciplinary ALS clinic for SLP, dietetics, respiratory, and social-work input.
Order an ALS-focused genetic panel (C9orf72, SOD1, TARDBP, FUS, TBK1) and arrange genetic counseling.
contraindicated_actions: Do not commit the patient to cervical spine surgery on the basis of incidental spondylotic changes when EMG findings extend beyond the cervical cord.
Do not start chronic immunosuppression (steroids, IVIG, plasma exchange) for ALS — there is no benefit and treatment delays correct diagnosis.
Do not defer respiratory assessment in a symptomatic patient — even mild FVC reduction warrants close monitoring and NIV planning.
Do not dismiss bulbar or progressive symptoms as functional / psychiatric without a complete neurological workup.
key_reasoning_points: Diagnosis requires evidence of both upper-motor-neuron involvement (hyperreflexia, Babinski, Hoffman, brisk jaw jerk, spasticity) and lower-motor-neuron involvement (atrophy, fasciculations, EMG denervation) with progressive spread, while excluding mimics — Awaji 2008 / Gold Coast 2020.

EMG in bulbar plus ≥2 spinal regions documenting fibrillations, positive sharp waves, complex fasciculation potentials, and large-amplitude long-duration polyphasic MUPs with reduced recruitment satisfies the electrodiagnostic criterion.
Normal sensory NCS and absence of conduction block are pivotal: they exclude common mimics including multifocal motor neuropathy, CIDP, and Kennedy disease.
Mild-to-moderate CK elevation (2–5× ULN) is consistent with ALS and does not itself indicate a primary myopathy.
Cervical spondylotic changes on MRI are common incidental findings in the at-risk age group; bulbar findings or multi-region EMG denervation cannot be attributed to cervical disease.
Baseline FVC, MIP/MEP, and SNIP/NIF inform NIV timing — NIV initiation at FVC <50% predicted or SNIP <40 cmH₂O prolongs survival and improves quality of life.
Young-onset or family history justifies genetic testing — C9orf72 is the most common cause and has implications for FTD risk and family counseling; SOD1 carriers may be eligible for tofersen.

July 2026 review applied end to end: EMG/NCS is the required ALS-specific test; brain and cord MRI and targeted labs exclude mimics; respiratory function is a recommended safety baseline; genetics is separately offered after counselling; CSF is absent except in five atypical mimic work-ups.

red_herrings.data_point: Anxiety / hypervigilance about ALS family history
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent to attribute paresthesias and twitching to anxiety / somatic hyperawareness
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Anxiety can mimic fasciculations but does not produce EMG-documented active denervation in 3+ regions

metadata.notes: Diagnostic puzzle: familial ALS (C9orf72) presenting in context of thyrotoxicosis and health anxiety. Thyroid normalization required before EMG interpretation; genetic testing reveals pathogenic expansion. Most complex ALS diagnostic scenario.
metadata.revision_reason: independent ALS review: targeted CSF/labs, separate optional genetics, EMG diagnostic, respiratory safety baseline, brain+cord MRI
